Real interaction · Experimental platforms

Learning and working with Spot

Two complementary platforms: directing a mobile robot, and learning to verify LLM-generated plans.

Walk along with Spot

In a 2 × 2 within-subject experiment, 218 operators controlled Spot using voice or gestures while standing or walking alongside it. HoloLens 2 supplied speech and hand-tracking inputs to the robot interface. The study included 872 real-robot trials.

Voice with walking was the most favoured combination. Gesture control while standing caused more left/right confusion, showing how physical position and command modality affect interaction.

LLM robotics workshop

A mobile web interface lets students submit navigation prompts and inspect plans, trajectories and rule-based penalties. Ten workshop sessions involved 226 students and culminated in live Spot demonstrations. Of 494 consented prompts, 457 entered the reported plan evaluation; 200 students provided the analysed questionnaire responses.

On Task 1, the reasoning-model condition achieved 55.7% penalty-free plans, compared with 18.7% in the non-reasoning condition. The reasoning condition fell to 21.6% on Task 3. Students changed their prompting strategies across conditions.

The workshop supports studying how people allocate work between themselves and an AI system. Reported learning is self-reported; the study did not establish long-term retention or isolate reasoning as an architectural cause of the model differences.

Shared principle: make the consequences of human instructions and AI decisions visible enough to inspect, discuss and measure.
